- When sentiment is consistently low (≤0.27) over recent days, model tends to overestimate prices; reduce forecast by 2–5% relative to prior 7-day average.
- After a sharp price spike (≥5% above recent mean), model often overshoots; cap forecast at +3% above peak or use 14-day moving average as ceiling.
- If sentiment is high (≥0.77) and price is trending up, model frequently overcorrects; apply downward bias of 1–3% to avoid overbought overreaction.
- When true outcome shows mean reversion (price drops 5%+ from recent peak), model often fails to recognize it; adjust forecast to align with 30-day rolling mean if deviation >3%.
- If sentiment is mixed (0.27–0.53) and price is volatile, model tends to overfit short-term noise; use 18-day smoothing filter to dampen erratic forecasts.
- For horizon >14 days, model often underestimates downward corrections; add 1–2% downward adjustment if sentiment is neutral or negative.
